value.body: An aircraft structures technician inspects and repairs the airframe (skins, frames, panels and composite parts) following the manufacturer's repair manuals. MRO organisations, airline maintenance bases and aerospace manufacturers hire for this work. A typical shift involves inspections during checks, repairing damage or corrosion, and documenting every task for sign-off.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: DGCA-approved AME course or aeronautical diploma

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Riveting tools, inspection aids, repair manuals

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most join an MRO or airline as a trainee technician after an AME course and build logged experience under supervision. DGCA licence modules under CAR-66 come later and widen what you can certify.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Reading structural repair manuals and drawings

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: licensed engineer (B1), structures inspector, shop supervisor.
Hangar work in shifts, including nights.
Hiring follows airline fleet and MRO activity, so it varies year to year.
